reason: Concrete Wry IPC/store boundary; payload-free ID selection and retention are tested in RequestLogStore, but a headless mock cannot supply this desktop AppHandle.
Native window visibility calls require the real window manager; the may_hide decision and stale frontend callbacks are tested independently.

Native recording command wiring requires Wry, capture and application stores. The delegated journal preparation, file-backed duration, recovery ownership, stale-session cancellation, retry replacement and waveform IPC are exercised without hardware.

HistoryData contains only serializable plain fields; serde_json has no reachable failure for this owned snapshot. Successful and failed retry commits, title preservation, correction protection, disk-write rollback and post-commit cleanup failure are exercised in storage tests.
Paste shortcut argument forwarding into OS input injection; chord order and cleanup are tested with a recording keyboard backend.

Concrete desktop IPC wrappers invoke the OS compositor on a blocking worker. Parser, privacy and program-picker behavior have deterministic tests; compositor availability is a native acceptance check.
Wry settings-store and actual foreground-process lookup glue. Profile resolution, explicit system override, invalid-value inheritance and serialization are unit-tested in this module.
Native application orchestration wires the tested session epoch, paste profile and visibility decisions into real shortcut/window callbacks.
Window event emission and the long-lived native waveform loop require the desktop event loop; notification ownership, waveform smoothing and listener teardown are independently tested.

Concrete Wry realtime event/clipboard bridge plus second ownership checks under mutex and poisoned-lock recovery. Exercising those check-between-check races would require nondeterministic scheduling or production test hooks. Streaming success/fallback, delayed connection/timeout and cancellation preserving the next session are tested.

Successful managed-auth refresh needs the native credential store and a Supabase session; the post-refresh cancellation-under-lock defense is race-only. Missing-session failure cleanup, token-error classification and STT retry behavior are tested.

Two cancellation guards inside hashing/between worker completion and upload are race-only. Boundary cancellation, cancellation during sample read, checkpoint resume and complete chunk assembly are tested. Listed function-only exceptions are duplicate LLVM generic instances, not source-body waivers.

LLVM emits uncalled generic copies for early-return/cancelled/native callers. These source functions and every changed line execute in successful routing, rewrite, unavailable-provider and cancellation tests; only duplicate function records may be waived.
Native paste-shortcut argument forwarding into UIA/clipboard output, protected by pure output-intent and chord tests.
Native best-effort cost event adapter receives no audio for OCR-only usage; this concrete AppHandle call requires desktop acceptance.

Concrete Wry history/log/cost finalization adapters now forward duration rather than decoding a whole recording. Duration extraction, activity metadata and log finalization semantics are independently tested.
Read a non-secret paste setting from the concrete Wry store. Parser/default/inheritance/persistence tests cover the delegated value semantics.
Window-manager hide callback; tested may_hide predicate prevents active recording from disappearing.
Actual foreground-process and OS paste-chord forwarding require a desktop; resolver and key-order tests cover the decisions.
Native retry output forwards the captured paste shortcut; pipeline replay and profile resolution are tested independently.

Concrete AppHandle cost-emission adapter converting optional WAV metadata to duration. Memory/file duration metadata is exercised by recording tests; actual native cost emission remains a desktop acceptance check.

Actual arboard clipboard read/OS wait cannot run safely in ordinary tests without touching the user's clipboard. Deterministic barrier tests cover immediate confirmation, busy/stale retries and fail-closed exhaustion; duplicate generic instance exception requires a covered source definition.

Real arboard/Enigo input and OS clipboard side effects are excluded from headless tests. Paste chord order/modifier cleanup, output policy and clipboard verification are tested at their owned boundaries.

Actual GNOME/KWin/X11/Sway/Hyprland IPC and uncommon OS temp-file/process errors require their desktop or fault injection. Backend selection, all response parsers, title opt-in/self filtering, helper failures, bounded output and malformed UTF-8 are covered. The ignored KWin smoke is intentionally not claimed as run.
Unused shortcut parameter in the Linux no-UIA fallback; actual Windows UIA requires Windows-native acceptance. Clipboard/key fallback logic has deterministic tests.

No executable Linux body: this selector re-exports the tested Linux implementation. Changed Windows Result wrapper and unsupported-platform fallback require their native target. Only these exact changed declarations may lack Linux coverage records.
